streak_freeze.note: 12 en keys (streakFreeze.*, paywall.benefit.streak.detail, widgets.streak.copy.frozen.*, widgets.streak.a11y.frozen); no fi copy ships, so this is a seed. The head noun stands alone on purpose: the compound that would name the streak ('putken jäädytys') waits for the open decision streak_term. forms lists the singular and plural cases UI copy produces; it cannot cover compounds the batch invents ('jäädytyspäivä') or the verb 'jäädyttää', so a term count is a floor, not a total. forbidden marks the food-freezer literal, which no string in this app can legitimately want.

task.note: Apple's own fi for Task (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/WorkflowKit.framework | Localizable.strings | Task (Parameter Label); Tasks -> Tehtävät in System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/DataAccess.framework | DataAccess.strings | AUTOGENERATED_MAIN_TASKS_TITLE). Governs focusTask.*, plan.*, widgets.tasks.*, insights.mood.completedTasks. forms covers the everyday cases plus the focus-task compound, including illative, allative and the 2sg possessive on the compound to match the bare noun's coverage — the possessive suffix is this app's most common imported shape (177 en keys carry a 2nd-person possessive, references/locale-briefs/fi.md '## Audience and register'), so a plausible line like 'Palaa keskittymistehtävääsi' needs to register as this term. forms still cannot cover every compound a batch forms (tehtäväkortti, tehtävälista), so read the drift list too. 'aktiviteetti' is the loan a translator reaches for and is never right here; it does not collide with Apple's 'aktiivisuustiedot' for activity data, which is a different word.

restricted_list.note: The named set of apps and categories blocked during a session (screenTime.createRestrictedList.*, screenTime.restrictedAppsPicker.*, plan.createToDo.removeRestrictedApps, plan.createToDo.restrictedAppsSection, focusTask.createTask.restrictedAppsSectionTitle). Chosen for width and plainness: 'esto' is what happens, and the compound is one word where 'lista estetyistä apeista' is four. If the open decision app_noun lands on 'sovellus', this term is unaffected because it names no app. forbidden marks the blacklist calque the concept note rules out; it cannot catch a paraphrase such as 'rajoitettujen appien lista', which is drift the editor reports.

time_value.note: Focused time priced at the user's own rate, shown as money and never received (insights.savings.*, achievements.category.wages.*, widgets.cash.*, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, onboarding.with*Moneyfesting.*). 'arvo' is Apple's own fi for Value (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/HealthRecordsUI.framework | HealthRecordsUI-Localizable.strings | MEDICAL_RECORD_DETAIL_TITLE_VALUE). forms lists the two-word phrase in the cases the labels need; a compound the batch may coin ('aika-arvo') is a finance term for something else and is drift, not a form. forbidden holds the two outcome nouns nearest to this concept; whole-word matching means 'ansio' does not hit the everyday postposition 'ansiosta', but a plain grep for the stem will, which the brief's Money frame records.

time_value_disclaimer.note: The fixed sentence after a time-value figure, on 11 en keys (achievements.badge.*.earned (7), achievements.category.wages.description, widgets.cash.description, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). The four sibling source sentences keep their own single fi form, listed in references/locale-briefs/fi.md '## Money frame'. forbidden is empty because no fi variant has shipped yet; the first batch's variants, if any, become forbidden rows. A paraphrase is what this list cannot catch: term_audit counts the approved sentence and says nothing about a line that reworded it, so the adjudicator compares every disclaimer key against this string.

hourly_rate.note: The rate the user sets to price their own time (onboarding.hourlyWage.*, profile.hourlyWage.*, currency.settings.*, screenTimeReport.missingWage, achievements.category.wages.description). 'hinta' is Apple's own fi for Price (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/StoreKitUI.framework | Gifting.strings | GIFTING_CONFIRM_PRICE_LABEL). 'tuntipalkka' is correct Finnish for an hourly wage and exactly the wrong word here, because the app pays nobody; en says 'hourly wage' on several keys, so a translator will reach for it, which is why it is forbidden rather than merely discouraged. The badge names in the payroll family are a metaphor and may use palkka-words; running copy may not.

daily_focus_goal.note: The daily minutes target drawn as a ring, met or not met (onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.*, profile.focusTarget.*, widgets.focusRing.*). 'tavoite' is Apple's own fi for Goal (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable-Eucalyptus.strings | SLEEP_MULTIPLE_GOAL_AXIS). forms lists the compound and the bare noun, so counts include keys that say only 'tavoite'. forbidden is empty on purpose: the words a wrong draft would use ('päämäärä', 'maali') are correct everyday Finnish that onboarding.personalGoal.* and the quote surfaces may legitimately need for an aspiration, so banning them would fire on correct copy. The bare 'tavoite' form is not scoped to this concept's keys, so a personalGoal string that happens to use 'tavoite' for an aspiration is credited here too and needs the same manual read the forbidden-field note asks for on the other side; term_audit's per-key breakdown is how the adjudicator tells the two apart.

minute_unit.note: The compact minute unit, spaced by default and glued only on a render verdict (common.durationMinuteUnit, insights.sessions.durationMinuteUnit, widgets.startFocus.minuteUnit, share.duration.minutesShort and minutesOnly, screenTimeReport.durationMinutesOnly, widgets.streak.focusedInStreak, widgets.streak.focusedMinutesSummary, moneyfesting.details.timeElapsedFormat, component.templateTaskCard.duration). Kielitoimiston ohjepankki gives min without a full stop and t, not h, for the hour (https://kielitoimistonohjepankki.fi/ohje/ajanilmaukset-lyhenteet-ajan-yksikot-ja-viikonpaivat/, fetched 2026-09-16), and Foundation prints '1 t 45 min' for fi_FI. forbidden is empty because the drift form is the single letter 'm', and a one-letter forbidden entry would fire on anything; a bare 'm' or 'h' left from en is an editor finding, recorded in the brief's Short forms table instead.

screen_time.note: Apple's fi name for the feature (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Screen Time; System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | ScreenTimeControllerTitle), on the 18 en keys that name it. What this list cannot cover: Finnish uses the same word for the generic notion of time spent on a screen, and term_audit matches case-insensitively, so a count here mixes the feature (capital R, e.g. insights.appUsage.title) with the generic sense (lower case, e.g. screenTimeReport.noData, insights.savings.estimateExplanation). Only the English name is forbidden; 'näyttöaika', the calque, is drift for the editor to report, not a forbidden form, because it is ordinary Finnish elsewhere.

forecast.note: The month-end projection of time value (insights.savings.forecast, insights.savings.*EstimateExplanation, insights.appUsage.permissionDescription, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*). Finnish keeps this apart from the month-end figure without effort: 'ennuste' is the forecast and 'arvio' the estimate (insights.savings.monthEnd, insights.savings.estimated), so the ro open decision 'forecast' has no fi counterpart. VoiceOver reads the two one after the other, so they must stay two words. forbidden marks the two nouns that would turn an estimate into a claim; 'takuu' is also a banned outcome word in the brief's Money frame.

Cancel.note: Apple's fi label for Cancel in both UIKit and SwiftUI (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Cancel; System/Library/Frameworks/SwiftUI.framework | Localizable.strings | Cancel); Undo is 'Peru', so the two do not collide

Done.note: Apple's fi Home Screen pill is also 'Valmis' (SpringBoardHome.strings | DONE), so unlike ro the mirror and the generic control share one form

Save.note: imperative on the plan badge ('Säästä 56 %', paywall.onboardingSubscription.annualPlanBadge); Finnish controls are second-person singular imperatives

Edit.note: meanwhile form: Apple's fi value for the Home Screen EDIT key is the literal '+', so the mirror has no word to copy (open decision edit_pill_label)

Retry.note: 'Try Again' takes the same preferred form; 'Uudelleen' is Apple's own narrow-button value (SpringBoard.strings | ACTIVATION_FAILED_RETRY_BUTTON)

Settings.note: Apple's fi uses one label for both 'Open Settings' and 'Go to Settings'; inside a sentence the app name inflects ('Asetuksissa'). setup_imperative replaces an earlier noun-stack draft ('käyttöönotto'), a bureaucratic verbal noun the brief's own register table flags as an imported shape

open.recommended_reason: It is the only option that means an unbroken run on its own, and it is short enough for the widget headers and the uppercase caption where this concept mostly lives.
open.note: No fi copy exists, so all three counts are 0. Keys: widgets.streak.* (about 30), share.card.streak*, streakFreeze.* (11), paywall.benefit.streak.*, onboarding.welcome.slide.streak.*, insights.summary.dayStreakTitle, achievements.streak.*. Evidence per option: 'putki' is the colloquial Finnish word for an unbroken run and gives PÄIVÄPUTKI for the DAY STREAK caption; 'jakso' is the head of Apple's own streak compound (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/Health/Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/MonthlyAchievements/localization/challenge/MoveStreak_SMALL_INCREASE | Localizable.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_ALERT_DESCRIPTION/NSStringLocalizedFormatKey 'arkiliikuntajakso') but on its own means any period, not an unbroken one; 'sarja' reads as a sequence of items rather than of days. Meanwhile agents write the days instead of the noun ('%lld päivää peräkkäin'), never choose per string, and the adjudicator lists every key that touched the concept; no terms row is added until this closes. Decide before the first fi batch; a flip afterwards is a global term change with its own follow-up batch.

Evidence per option: 'keskittyä' is Apple's verb for focusing (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/CoreServices/AccessibilityUIServer.app/Extensions/AccessibilityAppIntents.appex | Localizable.strings | BACKGROUND_SOUNDS_DESCRIPTION 'auttaa sinua keskittymään'); 'istunto' is Apple's noun for Session (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SensorKitUI.framework/AuthGroups/ECG.bundle | InfoPlist.strings | Session); 'fokus' has no Apple string. About 30 keys: screenTime.restrictedApps.appsRestricted, screenTime.createRestrictedList.appCount, insights.sessions.blockedAppsCount, profile.sessionDetails.blockedAppsCount, insights.appUsage.*, widgets.startFocus.openApp, onboarding.widgets.intro.appIconInstruction, onboarding.screenTimePermission.message and alertMessage. Evidence per option: 'appi' is Apple's own fi word throughout iOS (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | REMOVE_APP_SHORTCUT_ITEM_TITLE 'Poista appi', SHARE_APPLICATION_SHORTCUT_ITEM_TITLE 'Jaa appi'; Applications/FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL 'appien ja sivustojen käyttöä'; Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Home Screen & App Library 'Koti-valikko ja appikirjasto'); 'sovellus' is the general Finnish word most non-Apple software uses and is longer in every case form, which costs width on the widget and picker lines. Meanwhile agents use 'appi' so the pilot batch stays internally consistent, the adjudicator lists every key that carries it, and a flip is one follow-up batch, never a per-string choice.

open.recommended_reason: The point of the how-to is that the illustration matches the reader's own Home Screen, and no test pins a value on these two keys for any language.
open.note: Keys: onboarding.widgets.howTo.editPillLabel, drawn on the illustrated pill (Manifesting/Features/Onboarding/Business/WidgetsHowTo/View/HomeScreenJiggleIllustrationView.swift), and onboarding.widgets.howTo.step2 ('Tap Edit in the top corner, then Add Widget.'). Rule: an illustrated iOS label mirrors the device verbatim and a step that quotes it describes what the user actually sees. Apple's fi value for the Home Screen EDIT key is the literal '+' (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | EDIT), so there is no Finnish word to mirror; 'Muokkaa' is Apple's fi for the Customize menu item (same table, EDIT_MENU_CUSTOMIZE) and labels a button no Finnish iPhone shows in that position. Choosing '+' means rewriting step2 to name the control by shape ('Napauta yläkulman +-painiketta ja valitse sitten Lisää widgetti.') and a render check of the pill, which is far narrower than 'Edit'. Meanwhile the two keys stay unwritten in fi and the batch that reaches this screen reports the mismatch instead of guessing.

open.recommended_reason: The same onboarding step raises the real alert moments later, and a preview in another shape shows the reader a screen iOS will not.
open.note: Keys: onboarding.screenTimePermission.alertTitle, alertMessage, alertDoNotAllow; onboarding.notificationPermission.alertTitle, alertMessage, alertAllow, alertDoNotAllow; the Screen Time mock's Continue is the shared common.continue, quoted by onboarding.alert.screenTimeMessage. Rule: a mock of an iOS alert mirrors the device verbatim. Apple's fi differs from the en mocks in three ways (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: Applications/FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_TITLE, NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL, COMMON_CONTINUE, COMMON_DONT_ALLOW; System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_TITLE, USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_BODY, PERMISSION_ALERT_ALLOW, PERMISSION_ALERT_DENY): no quotation marks around the app name, a conditional Screen Time message ('Jos %@ saa luvan käyttää Ruutuaikaa, se saattaa voida nähdä aktiivisuustietosi...') instead of the en imperative, and a capitalised 'Asetuksissa' where en writes lower-case 'settings'. The options above are the two title shapes, so the counts read as a quote check. A yes costs a Continue key of its own instead of the shared common.continue (a code change) and a source flag first, because both en messages already differ from Apple's English. Meanwhile the seven keys stay unwritten in fi and findings go to an audit scope the owner names.

open.recommended_reason: The suffix sits directly against a money figure the money frame already asks readers to read carefully, and a Latin 'k' beside '€' reads as a bug.
open.note: An engineering finding, not a copy choice, recorded here because agents meet it in packets. AppCurrency.formatCompact appends a hardcoded Latin 'k', 'm' or 'b' (Manifesting/Foundation/Localization/AppCurrency.swift:53-56), so fi renders '1,25k €' and '1,25m €', while fi_FI's own compact tokens from Foundation's Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency(...).notation(.compactName) are 't.', 'milj.' and 'mrd.' ('1,25 t. €', '1,25 milj. €'). Surfaces: widgets.focusRing.row.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*, insights.savings.*, screenTimeReport.*, and the insights, celebration and session screens. Using the locale's notation changes the formatter for every locale, not just fi. Meanwhile agents never translate around the suffix, never spell it into copy, and report it once per batch that renders a compact amount; accessibility labels use the full format and are unaffected.
